notes: Scope: tax year 2025, single filer, no dependents, under 65, not blind, full-year resident, income = wages only. The calculator should treat wages as federal AGI (no pre-tax 401(k)/HSA/cafeteria deductions are modeled); for state_defined starting points wages are also the state base unless noted (e.g., NJ taxes 403(b)/457 contributions; MA allows a FICA deduction).

Bracket convention: each entry's 'min' is the lower bound of taxable income for that rate; the rate applies to income above 'min' up to the next entry's 'min'. Rates are decimals. Thresholds are the SINGLE-filer schedule in dollars of state taxable income (or federal taxable income where starts_from = federal_taxable_income).

standard_deduction and personal_exemption hold the single-filer value that applies at about $40,000 of wages. Where a value phases with income, or the bracket table alone does not reproduce the official tax, the state has an optional structured key ('phaseouts', 'alt_brackets', 'federal_tax_deduction', 'recapture', 'other_deductions', 'nyc_resident_brackets') and the rule is described in 'notes'. Optional keys added beyond the requested schema: additional_source_urls, changes_vs_2024, and those structured keys.

STATES WHERE THE PLAIN FIELDS ARE NOT ENOUGH AT $20k-$120k (calculator must implement the structured rule): OH (schedule base amounts: $342.00 + 2.75% over $26,050 and $2,394.32 + 3.125% over $100,000 -- plain brackets understate tax by $342; exemption steps $2,400/$2,150/$1,900 by MAGI; $20 credit); CT (exemption phase-out $15,000 to $0 between CT AGI $30,000 and $44,000; 2% rate add-back above $56,500; recapture above $105,000; personal tax credit table to $64,500); UT (no deduction -- 6% taxpayer credit on the $15,750 federal standard deduction, phased out at 1.3% above $18,213); WI (sliding standard deduction $13,560 minus 12% of income above $19,549); OR (federal income tax subtraction up to $8,500; $256 exemption credit lost above $100,000 federal AGI); MO (federal income tax deduction, 35%-0% of federal tax by AGI, cap $5,000); AL (uncapped federal income tax deduction; standard deduction $3,000 phasing to $2,500 between AL AGI $26,000 and $35,500); AR (Additional Tax Credit up to $60 for net taxable income up to $27,600; recapture band and higher-income formula above net taxable income $94,700, i.e., wages above about $97,170); NY (tax-benefit recapture above NY AGI $107,650; household credit up to $28,000); NM (low- and middle-income exemption up to $2,500 for AGI up to $36,667); MD (personal exemption $1,600 for federal AGI $100,001-$125,000); ME (standard deduction phase-out above Maine AGI $100,000); MA ($2,000 FICA/retirement deduction for every wage earner); KY (Family Size Tax Credit for MGI up to $20,815). Federal tax must be computed first for AL, MO and OR.

OBBBA conformity (federal 2025 standard deduction raised from $15,000 to $15,750 by P.L. 119-21 sec. 70102): states whose 2025 computation uses $15,750 -- AZ, CO, IA, ID, MO, MT, ND, NM (and UT's credit base). States tied to the federal amount that decoupled and use $15,000 -- SC, ME, DC (DC's is now a DC-defined amount). Federal Schedule 1-A deductions (tips, overtime, car-loan interest, senior) reduce state income in CO, IA, MT, ND (start from federal taxable income) and are separately subtracted in AZ and ID for 2025; they are NOT applied anywhere in this file, consistent with the federal treatment.

typical_local_income_tax_rate: for AL (0.0009), IA (0.0009), KY (0.0131), MD (0.0251), MI (0.0018), MO (0.0021), NY (0.0168), OH (0.0149) and PA (0.0107) the value is the Tax Foundation 2025 table footnote (a) statewide average effective local income tax rate as a percentage of AGI (2022 IRS/Census data), i.e., averaged over all residents including those in localities with no tax; apply it to wages/AGI. For IN the field is 0.0174, a population-weighted mean of 2025 statutory county rates (see Indiana notes), because TF's 0.49% conflicts with the statutory county taxes every resident pays. All other states are 0; flat per-head levies (e.g., Denver OPT, PA Local Services Tax, WV city service fees) and narrow city wage taxes (e.g., Wilmington DE 1.25%) are described in notes only. Each state's notes give statutory rates for major localities (e.g., NYC brackets, Philadelphia 3.74%-3.75%, Detroit 2.4%, MD counties 2.25%-3.30%).

Excluded from all figures: EITCs and other refundable or targeted credits (renter, property-tax, sales-tax, food credits; Oregon kicker; Idaho $10 Permanent Building Fund tax is noted but not included), payroll taxes (FICA, CA SDI 1.2%, WA Cares, MA PFML, Oregon statewide transit tax 0.1%), and capital gains/surtaxes outside the wage range.

Tax tables vs. formulas: many states (and the IRS below $100,000 of taxable income) require tax tables computed at the midpoint of $50 or $100 bands; a bracket formula differs from the official table by a few dollars at most.

Verification: every state entry marked verified = true had its rates, brackets, standard deduction and exemption confirmed from official tax-year-2025 state sources (2025 return instructions, rate schedules, tax tables, statutes or revenue-department publications) downloaded in October 2026, and was cross-checked against the Tax Foundation 2025 table (as of Jan 1, 2025). Secondary-source items (some local rates, some 2024 comparison figures, future-year changes) are identified as such in each state's notes and do not affect the 2025 state parameters.

Places where the Tax Foundation 2025 table (as of Jan 1, 2025) is superseded by official 2025 values: GA 5.19% (not 5.39%; HB 111 retroactive); SC top rate 6.0% (not 6.2%); OH top rate 3.125% (not 3.5%; HB 96) plus omitted base amounts; WI 4.4% bracket extended to $50,480 (2025 Act 15); ID 5.3% (not 5.695%), zero band $4,811, SD $15,750; UT 4.5% (not 4.55%), credit base $945/$18,213; MD standard deduction flat $3,350 (not $2,700) and new 6.25%/6.5% brackets; VA standard deduction $8,750 (not $8,500); CA, OR, VT, AR thresholds/deductions/credits indexed for 2025 (TF showed 2024 values); AZ, CO, IA, MO, MT, ND, NM standard deduction $15,750 (not $15,000); CT exemption phase-out reaches $0 above $44,000; IN local rate (see above).

federal.notes: Brackets: Rev. Proc. 2024-40, sec. 3.01 Table 3 (unmarried individuals), taxable-income thresholds for 2025; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, P.L. 119-21, signed July 4, 2025) made the TCJA rate structure permanent but did not change the 2025 thresholds, and the 2025 Form 1040 instructions' Tax Computation Worksheet (Section A, single) uses the same 103,350 / 197,300 / 250,525 / 626,350 breakpoints. Taxable income below $100,000 is taxed from the IRS Tax Table, which uses the midpoint of each $50 band; a formula on the brackets differs from the Table by at most a few dollars. Standard deduction: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 set the 2025 single amount at $15,000; OBBBA sec. 70102 amended IRC 63(c)(7) to $15,750 (single/MFS), $31,500 (MFJ), $23,625 (HOH), effective for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2024. The 2025 Form 1040 instructions use $15,750. The additional standard deduction for age 65+/blind ($2,000 unmarried) does not apply to the modeled filer. Personal exemption: $0 (permanently, under OBBBA). NEW 2025-2028 DEDUCTIONS, DESCRIBED BUT NOT APPLIED (all claimed on Schedule 1-A, flow to Form 1040 line 13b, so they reduce taxable income, not AGI, and are available to non-itemizers): (1) 'No tax on tips': deduction for qualified tips (occupations on the IRS list of those customarily and regularly receiving tips), capped at $25,000 per return; the cap is reduced by $100 for each full $1,000 of modified AGI over $150,000 (single; $300,000 MFJ); requires a valid SSN; married filers must file jointly; not available for specified service trades or businesses. (2) 'No tax on overtime': deduction for qualified overtime compensation, meaning only the FLSA section 7 premium portion (the 'half' of time-and-a-half), capped at $12,500 (single; $25,000 MFJ); same $150,000 MAGI threshold and $100-per-$1,000 reduction; SSN and joint-filing rules as for tips. For 2025 the W-2 does not separately report these amounts (transition-year penalty relief), so taxpayers rely on their own records. (3) Also on Schedule 1-A and also not applied: car-loan interest deduction up to $10,000, reduced by $200 per $1,000 (rounded up) of MAGI over $100,000 single; senior deduction of $6,000 per person age 65+, reduced by 6% of MAGI over $75,000 single. Why this matters for states: states that start from federal AGI are unaffected by these deductions unless they adopt them; states that start from federal taxable income may pick them up depending on their conformity (see each state's notes). Credits not applied: the EITC for a filer with no qualifying children (2025 maximum $649) phases out completely at $19,104 of AGI (Rev. Proc. 2024-40 sec. 3.06), so it is zero across the $20k-$120k range. Payroll taxes (Social Security, Medicare, Additional Medicare) are not income taxes and are excluded.

Alabama.notes: Source: 2025 Form 40 booklet (ADOR). Order of computation (Form 40): Alabama AGI (line 10, state-defined gross income less AL adjustments) minus standard or itemized deduction (line 11) minus federal income tax deduction (line 12) minus personal exemption (line 13) minus dependent exemption (line 14) = taxable income (line 16). Single personal exemption: 'If you check box 1, enter $1,500 on line 13'. It is a deduction with no phase-out. Single standard deduction chart (page 9): $3,000 for AL AGI $0-$25,999, then $25 less for each $500 AGI band ($26,000-$26,499 gets $2,975, and so on), and $2,500 at $35,500 and above. That gives $3,000 at $20k wages and $2,500 at $40k, $80k and $120k. Federal income tax deduction worksheet (page 31): 2025 Form 1040 line 22 tax plus Form 8960 NIIT, minus EIC, additional child tax credit, refundable American Opportunity credit, refundable adoption credit and Form 2439 credits, floored at 0. No cap applies to individuals. Because the deduction uses actual 2025 federal liability, OBBBA changes ($15,750 federal standard deduction, tips/overtime deductions) shrink the federal tax and so the AL deduction, which raises AL tax slightly. The calculator should compute 2025 federal tax under post-OBBBA law and deduct it. Tax: under $100,000 taxable income, tax comes from a tax table in $50/$100 bands priced at the band midpoint. Spot checks: single tax is $1,128 at $23,300-$23,400 and $1,958 at $39,900-$40,000, matching 10 + 100 + 5% x (midpoint - 3,000). Over $100,000 the worksheet is 5% x (TI - 100,000) + $4,958, which is $2 below the exact bracket formula ($4,960 at $100,000). Matches Tax Foundation exactly for rates, brackets, standard deduction (TF footnote c describes the same phase-down) and exemption. Overtime: per the ADOR notice (Act 2023-421 as amended by Act 2024-437), FLSA overtime pay was excluded from AL gross income only through June 30, 2025. Exempt amounts are kept out of W-2 box 16 and reported in box 14 'EX OT WAGES'. An extension reportedly failed in the 2025 session (secondary source: Warren Averett). The act numbers come from secondary summaries. Alabama did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions; tips are taxable. No low-income credit for single filers. Local: TF footnote (a) gives a statewide average effective local income tax of 0.09% of AGI (2022 IRS/Census data), used as typical_local_income_tax_rate = 0.0009. Statutory local taxes are flat municipal or county occupational license taxes on gross wages, based on where the work is done. Examples from secondary sources (Alabama League of Municipalities survey as reported; not checked against ordinances): Birmingham 1%, Bessemer 1%, Gadsden/Attalla/Glencoe/Rainbow City/Southside 2%, Macon County 1%. About 26 jurisdictions are listed at 0.5%-2%. Per the 2025 booklet, local/occupational tax withheld cannot be counted as Alabama income tax withheld, but 'City, County, and Occupational Tax as reported on your W-2' can be deducted on Alabama Schedule A line 8. That helps only itemizers, not standard-deduction filers. verified = true covers state rates, brackets, standard deduction and exemption. Local rates are TF/secondary.
Alabama.changes_vs_2024: None material. 2024 Form 40 booklet has identical single values: 2%/4%/5% with breaks at $500 and $3,000, a $3,000 standard deduction phasing down to $2,500, and a $1,500 personal exemption. The only difference is that the state overtime exclusion covered all of 2024 but only Jan 1-Jun 30, 2025 (see notes).

phaseouts.applies_to: standard_deduction

Alaska.notes: No individual income tax (repealed 1980-81). No local income taxes. starts_from is not meaningful for no-tax states and is set to 'state_defined' as a placeholder.

Arizona.notes: Rate: flat 2.5% on Arizona taxable income (2025 Form 140 line 46: 'Multiply line 45 by 2.5%'). The optional tax table and the X/Y tables are obsolete. Standard deduction: the 2025 Form 140 booklet lists $15,750 single / $31,500 MFJ / $23,625 HOH. ADOR printed the booklet before the legislature acted and assumed Arizona would conform to post-1/1/2025 federal changes. Conformity was then enacted: HB 4168 (substituted for SB 1861), Laws 2026 Ch. 140, signed 6/13/2026. It amends A.R.S. 43-1041(A)(1) from $12,200 (indexed) to $15,750 for single, retroactive to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2024 (Sec. 35). It also amends A.R.S. 43-105 so that 2025 uses the IRC as of 1/1/2025 plus the P.L. 119-21 provisions that are retroactively effective for 2025. Statutory text was read from the House-engrossed version (HB4168H). The Senate as-enacted fact sheet confirms the $15,750 / $23,625 / $31,500 amounts as 'Retroactive to January 1, 2025'. So for 2025 the AZ amount equals the OBBBA federal $15,750, not $15,000. The Tax Foundation's $15,000 is pre-OBBBA. Charitable increase to the standard deduction for 2025 is 34% of the charitable deductions that would have been allowed if itemizing. For 2026+ Ch. 140 changes it to 100% of 170(c) contributions, capped at $1,000 single. Personal exemption: none for a single filer. Arizona replaced personal and dependent exemptions with a dependent credit of $100 under 17 and $25 at 17+, phasing out above $200k FAGI single. Age-65 and blind exemptions exist but are not relevant here. Low-income credits: the Family Income Tax Credit for a single filer with 0 dependents requires Arizona income of $10,000 or less ($40 credit), so it does not apply at $20k+. The Increased Excise Tax Credit is also low-income only. Neither is included. New for 2025 under Ch. 140, retroactive: subtractions for qualified tips, qualified overtime, the federal senior deduction, and qualified passenger-vehicle loan interest, each to the extent deducted federally. These are not modeled. If the model treats overtime as wages, AZ taxable income would be lower for overtime earners. Federal income tax is not deductible. No local income taxes in Arizona. Value at ~$40k wages: (40,000 - 15,750) x 2.5% = $606.25. Illustrative: $20k: $106.25; $80k: $1,606.25; $120k: $2,606.25. Tax Foundation discrepancies: TF lists std deduction $15,000 (pre-OBBBA federal amount); official 2025 is $15,750. TF footnote (e) cites 33% (TY2024) for the charitable add-on; 2025 is 34%. TF rate (2.5%) matches.
Arizona.changes_vs_2024: Single standard deduction rose from $14,600 (2024 Form 140 booklet) to $15,750 for 2025. The rate is unchanged at a flat 2.5%. Tax at $40k wages is $606.25 in 2025, down from $635.00 in 2024. The charitable add-on to the standard deduction rose from 33% to 34% of charitable contributions (not relevant for the typical filer).

Arkansas.notes: Income starting point is state-defined. AR1000F builds total income from W-2 wages (line 8) and other items; AR AGI (line 25) is total income minus Arkansas adjustments. Federal AGI is not the starting line. Net taxable income (NTI) = AGI minus the $2,470 standard deduction (single, 2025) or AR3 itemized deductions. Tax comes from the 2025 Regular Tax Table (Rev 09/29/2025; $100 bands, computed at band midpoints and rounded). DFA's 2025 Indexed Tax Brackets: 0% for $0-$5,599; 2% for $5,600-$11,199 (minus $111.98); 3% for $11,200-$15,999 (minus $223.97); 3.4% for $16,000-$26,399 (minus $287.97); 3.9% for $26,400-$94,700 (minus $419.96); then the recapture band and higher-income rules in alt_brackets. The minus-adjustment formulas equal bracket lower bounds of $5,599/$11,199/$15,999/$26,399. Using the listed 'From' values ($5,600 etc.) understates tax by at most $0.13. A script check reproduced all 948 $100 rows of the official 2025 Regular Tax Table ($5,000-$100,000) exactly at band midpoints using these formulas. The personal tax credit is $29 per taxpayer, nonrefundable (an extra $29 each for 65+, blind, deaf, or HoH/surviving spouse). Federal income taxes are not deductible (listed under taxes you cannot deduct). Arkansas has no local income taxes. Illustrative 2025 liability for a single filer with no dependents taking the standard deduction (formula values, then minus the $29 credit): $20k wages: NTI $17,530, tax about $308, minus $29, minus the $60 Additional Tax Credit = about $219. $40k: NTI $37,530, tax about $1,044, minus $29 = about $1,015. $80k: NTI $77,530, about $2,604 - $29. $120k: NTI $117,530, $3,809 + 3.9% x $17,530 = about $4,493 - $29. The Additional Tax Credit ($60 to $5) applies only up to NTI $27,600, i.e. wages up to about $30,070. Wages up to about $97,170 fall in the primary schedule (most of the $20k-$120k range). Above that, see alt_brackets. Tax Foundation discrepancies: TF's standard deduction of $2,410 is the 2024 figure (2025 is $2,470). TF's '2% > $0, 3.9% > $4,500' schedule and its footnote (g) thresholds ($5,300/$10,600/$15,100/$25,000/$89,600) and (kk) band ($89,600-$92,700) match neither DFA's official 2024 brackets ($5,500/$10,900/$15,600/$25,700; band $92,301-$95,500) nor 2025 ($5,600/$11,200/$16,000/$26,400; band $94,701-$97,800). TF's high-income form implies a $85.50 adjustment vs the official 2025 $89.30 (equivalent to 2% on the first $4,700, not $4,500). The $29 credit matches TF. DFA's 2025 materials show no 2025 legislation changing 2025 rates; the 'What's New in Sales Tax for 2025' document covers sales tax only.

alt_brackets.applies_when: Net taxable income (AGI minus standard deduction) $94,701-$97,800: bracket-adjustment (recapture) band. Wages of about $97,171-$100,270 at the standard deduction.
alt_brackets.bracket_adjustment_formula: tax = 0.039*NTI - adj, where adj = 399.30 - 10*floor((NTI - 94701)/100). adj is $399.30 for $94,701-$94,800 and falls $10 per $100 band to $99.30 for $97,701-$97,800 (DFA 2025 Indexed Tax Brackets).
tax = 0.039*NTI - 89.30. This is the same as 2% on the first $4,700 plus 3.9% above (0.019*4,700 = 89.30). The equivalence is derived; DFA presents only the minus-adjustment form.
Official rule: tax = $3,809 + 3.9% of the excess over $100,000, i.e. 0.039*NTI - 91.00. The $1.70 gap from the -$89.30 formula comes from the table's midpoint rounding at the $99,901-$100,001 row.

phaseouts.applies_to: Additional Tax Credit for Qualified Individuals (nonrefundable; AR1000TC line 6; Act 1 of 2021 2nd Ext. Sess.). Available to all filers by net taxable income, with no age or child requirement.
phaseouts.formula: credit = 60 if NTI <= 26,500; otherwise 60 - 5*ceil((NTI - 26,500)/100) for NTI $26,501-$27,600 ($55 down to $5); 0 if NTI >= $27,601. Single filers use the table once. Credits beyond tax are not refundable.

phaseouts.applies_to: Low Income Tax Table (single, Filing Status 1). It uses AGI with the standard deduction built in and replaces the regular table when eligible.
phaseouts.formula: Tax $0 if AGI <= $14,643; table runs to AGI $17,500 (tax $222 at $17,401-$17,500); above $17,500 use the standard deduction and the Regular Tax Table. Not applicable at wages of $20k or more.

Arkansas.changes_vs_2024: Inflation indexing only. Top rate is 3.9% in both years (Act 1 of 2024 2nd Ext. Sess.; the 2025 instructions say 2025 marginal rates are 3.9% as amended in 2024). Standard deduction rose from $2,410 to $2,470. Bracket starts moved from $5,500/$10,900/$15,600/$25,700 to $5,600/$11,200/$16,000/$26,400. The 3.9% minus-adjustment rose from $409.86 to $419.96. The recapture band moved from $92,301-$95,500 to $94,701-$97,800. The adjustment above the band rose from $87.40 to $89.30. The base tax at $100,000 changed from $3,811 to $3,809. The Additional Tax Credit ceiling rose from NTI $26,900 to $27,600 (full $60 up to $25,800 in 2024 vs $26,500 in 2025). The single low-income-table ceiling rose from $17,000 to $17,500. The $29 personal credit is unchanged. Net effect at $40k wages is about -$11 (about $1,026 in 2024 vs $1,015 in 2025, after the $29 credit).

California.notes: Schedule X (single) is from the FTB '2025 California Tax Rate Schedules': 1% to $11,079; 2% over $11,079; 4% over $26,264; 6% over $41,452; 8% over $57,542; 9.3% over $72,724; 10.3% over $371,479; 11.3% over $445,771; 12.3% over $742,953. The 13.3% entry at $1,000,000 is the 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax (formerly Mental Health Services Tax, Form 540 line 62) on taxable income over $1M, shown as a bracket to mirror Tax Foundation. Taxable income of $100,000 or less uses the FTB tax table, which approximates the schedule. Standard deduction: $5,706 single (2025 booklet, 'California Standard Deduction Chart for Most People'); no phase-out. Personal exemption: a $153 nonrefundable credit per Form 540 line 7 ('X $153'). Exemption credits are limited only when federal AGI exceeds $252,203 single, so there is no effect at $20k-$120k. Starting point: federal AGI (Form 540 line 13) with Schedule CA adjustments; CA uses its own standard deduction. The federal OBBBA below-AGI deductions (Schedule 1-A: tips, overtime, etc.) and the $15,750 federal standard deduction do not affect the CA computation. Federal tax is not deductible. Value at ~$40k wages: taxable income 34,294; schedule tax $414.49 + 4% x (34,294 - 26,264) = $735.69, less $153 = $582.69. Illustrative: $20k: $22.09; $80k: $3,194.98; $120k: $6,914.98. Not included: the Nonrefundable Renter's Credit ($60 single if CA AGI is $53,994 or less, renters only), CalEITC, the Young Child Tax Credit and the Foster Youth Tax Credit. Payroll (not income tax): SDI is 1.2% of all wages for 2025 with no wage cap since 2024 (EDD: 'The SDI withholding rate for 2025 is 1.2 percent'). No local income taxes on employee wages. Tax Foundation discrepancies: all TF CA values are 2024 figures per TF footnotes (j)/(n): brackets 10,756..., std deduction $5,540, credit $149. TF footnote (l) cites SDI at 1.1% (the 2024 rate); 2025 is 1.2%. TF's 2024 top thresholds ($360,659/$432,787/$721,314) are likewise superseded by $371,479/$445,771/$742,953.
California.changes_vs_2024: Brackets were indexed by about 3.0%. 2024 single thresholds: 2% from $10,756, 4% from $25,499, 6% from $40,245, 8% from $55,866, 9.3% from $70,606. 2025: $11,079 / $26,264 / $41,452 / $57,542 / $72,724. Standard deduction rose from $5,540 to $5,706. The personal exemption credit rose from $149 to $153. At $40k wages, tax falls from $611.86 (2024) to $582.69 (2025). Rates are unchanged. SDI (payroll, not income tax) rose from 1.1% to 1.2% of all wages.

Colorado.notes: 2025 Colorado Book 104 (10/29/25; DR 0104 rev. 10/03/25, i.e., after the Aug 2025 special session): line 1 = federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15), so the 2025 OBBBA $15,750 single SD and Schedule 1-A deductions are embedded; line 13 'The income tax rate is currently 4.4%'; tax table 'with tax rate of 4.4%'. CDOR Individual Income Tax Guide rate table: 2024 4.25%, 2025 4.4%. Tips: CDOR guide - 'No addback is required' for the federal qualified tips deduction (flows through). Overtime: HB25-1296 (signed 5/16/2025) created an addback of federal overtime deductions, but CDOR's guide states the addback applies 'For tax years 2026 and later' and the 2025 DR 0104 has no overtime addback line - so federal overtime deduction also reduces CO income for TY2025. Aug 2025 special session: HB25B-1001 made the QBI addback permanent from 2026 (QBI addback for AGI > $500k already applies in 2025; irrelevant for wages); other special-session bills mainly business/2026+. Line 4 standard/itemized deduction addback applies only if AGI > $300,000 (deduction above $12,000 single for 2025). HB26-1289 (2026) does not affect TY2025 individual rates. Value at $40k wages: FTI 24,250 x 4.4% = $1,067. Local: no local income tax; Denver occupational privilege tax $5.75/month employee ($69/yr; employer $4/month) per City of Denver page; a few other cities (e.g., Glendale, Greenwood Village, Sheridan) levy small flat monthly OPTs (amounts not verified) - flat per-head charges, so typical_local_income_tax_rate = 0. Not included: TABOR state sales tax refund claimed on DR 0104 line 38 for 2025, single: $19 (MAGI <= $52,000), $25 ($52,001-$105,000), $29 ($105,001-$168,000) - a TABOR refund, not an income-tax parameter; Colorado EITC and child credits; FAMLI paid-leave premium (payroll, not income tax). Discrepancy with Tax Foundation: TF SD $15,000 (pre-OBBBA); correct embedded 2025 amount is $15,750. Rate matches TF.
Colorado.changes_vs_2024: Rate 4.25% in 2024 (temporary TABOR-triggered reduction under C.R.S. 39-22-627) -> 4.40% in 2025 (no temporary reduction). Embedded federal SD $14,600 -> $15,750. Net: higher CO tax at a given wage above ~$48k (rate effect outweighs the larger SD; e.g., $40k: 2024 $1,079.50 vs 2025 $1,067.00; $120k: 2024 $4,479.50 vs 2025 $4,587.00).

Connecticut.notes: Source: CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25), Tax Calculation Schedule and Tables A-E, pp.18-22. Table B single: <= $10,000 2%; $10,000-50,000 $200 + 4.5%; $50,000-100,000 $2,000 + 5.5%; $100,000-200,000 $4,750 + 6%; $200,000-250,000 $10,750 + 6.5%; $250,000-500,000 $14,000 + 6.9%; > $500,000 $31,250 + 6.99%. The base amounts equal the cumulative marginal tax. Computation: CT AGI minus Table A exemption = TI; Table B tax + Table C add-back + Table D recapture; then multiply by (1 - Table E decimal). No standard deduction. The personal exemption is a deduction that phases out (see phaseouts). The required personal_exemption field holds the value at exactly $40,000 CT AGI ($5,000; it drops to $4,000 at $40,001). CT AGI = federal AGI (1040 line 11a) plus CT additions minus subtractions. Federal tax is not deductible. No tax if CT AGI <= $15,000 (single). CT tax tables may be used if CT AGI <= $102,000 (minor rounding differences). Examples (wages only, schedule method): $20k: exemption 15,000, TI 5,000, tax 100 x (1 - .60) = $40. $40k: exemption 5,000, TI 35,000, tax 1,325 x (1 - .10) = $1,192.50. $80k: TI 80,000, 3,650 + 125 add-back = $3,775. $120k: TI 120,000, 5,950 + 250 add-back + 75 recapture = $6,275. The property tax credit (up to $300; see phaseouts) is excluded because it depends on paying property tax, but it is common (car owners). It is capped at the income tax due, e.g. $40 at $20k wages. CT EITC not included. LOCAL: none. Differences from Tax Foundation: TF lists the $15,000 exemption without phase-out in the table (phase-out only in footnote r). Per Table A the exemption reaches $0 for CT AGI > $44,000, not at '$45,000+'. TF footnote (p) gives a single recapture maximum of $3,150, while 2025 Table D tops out at $3,400 for CT AGI > $540,000 (irrelevant at <= $120k). TF footnote (p)'s 2% phase-out ($25 per $5,000 above $56,500, max $250) and $105,000 recapture start match Tables C and D. The Table E credit schedule is not in TF; it is reproduced in phaseouts.
Connecticut.changes_vs_2024: None. The 2024 CT-1040 instructions have the same Table B rate schedule, and Tables A, C, D and E were verified identical, as were the property tax credit ($300, $49,500 single threshold) and the $15,000 no-tax threshold.

phaseouts.applies_to: Personal exemption (Table A), deduction from CT AGI
phaseouts.formula: exemption = 15000 if CT_AGI <= 30000; else max(0, 15000 - 1000*ceil((CT_AGI - 30000)/1000)). Zero for CT AGI > 44,000.

phaseouts.applies_to: 2% tax rate phase-out add-back (Table C), added to tax
phaseouts.formula: addback = 0 if CT_AGI <= 56500; else min(250, 25*ceil((CT_AGI - 56500)/5000)). Equivalent to taxing $1,000 of the 2% bracket at 4.5% per $5,000 step.

phaseouts.applies_to: Tax recapture (Table D), added to tax
Personal tax credit (Table E): tax after credit = (Table B tax + Table C + Table D) * (1 - decimal)
phaseouts.formula: Decimal by CT AGI (upper bounds inclusive; lower bound exclusive). For CT AGI <= 15,000 tax is 0 because the exemption covers all income.

phaseouts.applies_to: Property tax credit (Schedule 3), conditional on paying CT property tax on a primary residence and/or one motor vehicle; nonrefundable; NOT included in brackets
phaseouts.formula: credit = min(300, qualifying property tax paid, income tax) * (1 - decimal). Decimal = 0 if CT AGI <= 49,500, then .15/.30/.45/.60/.75/.90 per $10,000 band (49,500-59,500 = .15, ... 99,500-109,500 = .90), 1.00 above 109,500.

Delaware.notes: Rates: 30 Del. C. § 1102(a)(14), 'for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2013'. 0% on the first $2,000; 2.2% $2,000-5,000; 3.9% $5,000-10,000; 4.8% $10,000-20,000; 5.2% $20,000-25,000; 5.55% $25,000-60,000; 6.6% over $60,000. The same schedule applies to all filing statuses, and it is not indexed. Delaware Code Online shows no later paragraph; § 1102 was last amended by 79 Del. Laws c. 10. The 2025 PIT-RES instructions (revised 03/26/26) say to use the tax table if line 23 < $60,000 and the tax schedule at the end of the tax table otherwise. I did not retrieve that separate 2025 tax table document; the rates above come from the statute. Standard deduction: $3,250 single (2025 PIT-RES instructions line 20a; § 1108(a)(3)). Additional $2,500 for 65+/blind is irrelevant here. Personal credit: $110 per personal exemption (2025 instructions line 27a; § 1110(b)). It is nonrefundable: § 1110(c) says it cannot exceed tax. Starting point: federal AGI (PIT-RES line 1) +/- Delaware modifications. Example at $40k wages: taxable = 36,750; gross tax = 66 + 195 + 480 + 260 + 652.13 = $1,653.13; less $110 = $1,543. Local: Wilmington levies an earned income (wage) tax on residents' earned income and on nonresidents' income earned in the city. 22 Del. C. §§ 901-902 authorize this only for municipalities over 50,000 people and cap it at 1.25% for both residents and nonresidents. Wilmington is the only such Delaware city. The city's 1.25% rate is widely reported, but wilmingtonde.gov returned HTTP 403, so I could not confirm the rate on the city's own page. Statewide typical local rate set to 0. Not included: Delaware EITC (DE Schedule II), pension exclusion (irrelevant). No discrepancies with Tax Foundation.
Delaware.changes_vs_2024: None. The rate schedule (30 Del. C. § 1102(a)(14), in effect for all tax years after 2013), the $3,250 standard deduction (§ 1108) and the $110 personal credit (§ 1110(b)) are identical for 2024 and 2025.

Florida.notes: No personal income tax (Fla. Const. Art. VII, s. 5); no filing requirement for individuals. No local income taxes. starts_from is a placeholder.

Georgia.notes: Source: 2025 IT-511 booklet, which states 'Effective January 1, 2025, the income tax rate is 5.19%'. Form 500 line 16 is line 15c x 5.19%, rounded to the dollar. Form 500EZ is discontinued for 2025. Computation: federal AGI (line 8, 'Do not use Federal taxable income') +/- GA adjustments, minus the GA standard deduction ($12,000 single, flat, no phase-out; must be used if the taxpayer took the federal standard deduction) or itemized deductions, minus the $4,000-per-dependent exemption = taxable income. Georgia has no personal exemption for the taxpayer, repealed starting 2024 (2024 IT-511). Same values at $20k/$40k/$80k/$120k. Discrepancy with Tax Foundation: TF lists 5.39% as of Jan 1, 2025, which predates HB 111. Correct 2025 rate is 5.19%. Standard deduction ($12,000) and no exemption match TF. Low Income Credit (Form 500 line 17) requires federal AGI under $20,000, so it does not apply anywhere in $20k-$120k. Georgia Eligible Itemizer Credit (up to $300) is for itemizers only. Conformity: the 2025 IT-511 says GA conforms to the IRC as of Jan 1, 2025 and had not adopted OBBBA. Secondary sources (not checked against the bill text) say 2026 HB 1199 later moved conformity to Jan 1, 2026, but decoupled from the tips, overtime and car-loan deductions. These are below-AGI federal deductions in any case, and GA starts from federal AGI with its own standard deduction, so they do not reduce GA tax for 2025. 2026 HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026 per governor's release) lowers the rate to 4.99% and adds small tips/overtime exclusions for 2026-2028 only, so 2025 is unaffected. The one-time surplus rebates ($250 single) are refunds tied to prior-year returns, not 2025 rate parameters. No local income taxes.
Georgia.changes_vs_2024: Rate cut from 5.39% (2024 IT-511) to 5.19% for 2025, enacted retroactively to Jan 1, 2025 by HB 111 (signed April 15, 2025). The single standard deduction stays at $12,000 and there is no personal exemption in either year. Effect: 0.20 points on taxable income, e.g. about $56 less at $40k wages ($28,000 taxable).

Hawaii.notes: Source: Hawaii DOTAX 2025 Form N-11 instruction booklet ('2025 Tax Rate Schedules', Schedule I, single/MFS). Cumulative base taxes in the official schedule: $134 at 9,600; $288 at 14,400; $552 at 19,200; $859 at 24,000; $1,675 at 36,000; $2,539 at 48,000; $8,391 at 125,000; $12,341 at 175,000. Taxable income < $100,000 MUST use the Tax Table ($50 bands); the schedule gives the same result up to rounding. Standard deduction (N-11 line 23): $4,400 single. It is state-defined; Hawaii did not adopt the federal TCJA/OBBBA standard deduction amounts. Under Act 46 the next scheduled increase is TY2026. Personal exemption (line 25): $1,144, a deduction. Starting point: federal AGI (N-11 line 7) with Hawaii additions/subtractions to reach Hawaii AGI. Hawaii conforms to the IRC as of Dec 31, 2024 (Act 123, SLH 2025). The 2025 booklet's 'Changes to Note' lists no 2025 legislation altering 2025 rates, deductions or exemptions. Citation discrepancy: the N-11 booklet cites the bracket and standard deduction law as 'Act 45, SLH 2024', while DOTAX Tax Research ('Estimating the Impacts of Hawaii's 2024 Tax Cut Bill') identifies HB 2404 as Act 46, SLH 2024. The numbers are unaffected. Example at $40k wages: taxable = 40,000 - 4,400 - 1,144 = 34,456; tax = 859 + 6.8% x 10,456 = $1,570. Not included: refundable food/excise tax credit (single federal AGI < $40,000; Form N-311), credit for low-income household renters, refundable Hawaii EITC. No county/local income taxes. No discrepancies with Tax Foundation on any numeric value.
Hawaii.changes_vs_2024: Large change. Act 46, SLH 2024 (HB 2404) widened the single brackets for 2025. The 2024 single schedule was: 1.4% to $2,400; 3.2% to $4,800; 5.5% to $9,600; 6.4% to $14,400; 6.8% to $19,200; 7.2% to $24,000; 7.6% to $36,000; 7.9% to $48,000; 8.25% to $150,000; 9% to $175,000; 10% to $200,000; 11% above. The 2025 schedule is in brackets. The standard deduction ($4,400) and exemption ($1,144) are unchanged from 2024; the standard deduction had risen from $2,200 to $4,400 in 2024. Example at $40k wages: 2024 tax = $2,149, 2025 tax = $1,570.

Idaho.notes: Source: 2025 Idaho Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions, EIN00046 rev. 03-02-2026. What's New: 'Idaho conforms to the IRC as of January 1, 2026'. 'Effective January 1, 2025, the individual income tax rate is 5.3%.' Form 40 tax worksheet: (Idaho taxable income - $4,811 single [$9,622 MFJ/HOH]) x 5.3%. Idaho calls this a flat tax with a zero-rate band. It is coded here as two brackets (0% to $4,811, then 5.3%) and labeled 'graduated' so that bracket-iterating code handles the zero band; change the label to 'flat' if your code reads brackets regardless. Standard deduction: $15,750 single (Form 40 line 16 / standard deduction worksheet), i.e. Idaho uses the OBBBA federal amount for 2025. Conformity: HB 559 (2026 Sess. Laws ch. 1, signed 2/10/2026, retroactive to 1/1/2025) updated Idaho's IRC reference. Rate: HB 40 (2025 Sess. Laws ch. 13, signed 3/6/2025, retroactive to 1/1/2025). No personal exemption. Line 18 subtracts federal Form 1040 lines 13a+13b: the QBI deduction plus the federal Schedule 1-A deductions for tips, overtime, car-loan interest and the enhanced senior deduction. Overtime/tip earners therefore get the same deduction in Idaho; not modeled. Permanent Building Fund tax: a flat $10 is due from every filer required to file an Idaho return. This applies to all single filers at $20k-$120k, unless receiving Idaho public assistance or blind. It is not in the brackets; add $10 if desired. Food Tax Credit (formerly the Grocery Credit): $155 per person for 2025, claimed on line 43 under Payments and Other Credits, i.e. effectively refundable. It is not included (EITC-type). No local income taxes. Federal income tax is not deductible. Value at ~$40k wages: taxable income 24,250, tax 0.053 x (24,250 - 4,811) = $1,030.27, plus $10 PBF. $20k: $0 (taxable income $4,250 is below the zero band). $80k: $3,150.27. $120k: $5,270.27. Idaho tax tables are used for lower incomes and approximate the formula. Tax Foundation discrepancies: TF shows 5.695% (pre-HB 40; official 2025 is 5.3%), zero band $4,673 (2024; 2025 is $4,811), and std deduction $15,000 (2025 is $15,750). Structure label: Idaho itself calls this a flat tax; it is coded 'graduated' only because of the 0% band so that bracket-iterating code is used.
Idaho.changes_vs_2024: Rate cut from 5.695% to 5.3%, retroactive to 1/1/2025 (HB 40). The zero-rate band rose from $4,673 to $4,811 single. The standard deduction rose from $14,600 to $15,750 (Idaho conforms to IRC as of 1/1/2026, retroactive to 1/1/2025). At $40k wages, tax falls from $1,180.40 (2024) to $1,030.27 (2025), excluding the $10 PBF tax. The food (grocery) tax credit rose to $155 per person; the 2024 amount was not verified here.

Illinois.notes: 2025 IL-1040 Instructions, 'What's New for 2025': 'The Illinois income tax rate is 4.95 percent (.0495)' and 'The personal exemption amount for tax year 2025 is $2,850.' The 2025 IL-1040 line 12 multiplies line 11 by 4.95%. The exemption is a deduction from base income. If the filer can be claimed as a dependent, the exemption is $0 when base income exceeds $2,850 (not relevant here). It is denied entirely when federal AGI exceeds $250,000 for single filers (cliff). No standard deduction. Starts from federal AGI (IL-1040 line 1), so the federal tips/overtime deductions (below AGI) do not flow through. No local income taxes on individuals. Excluded credits: Illinois EITC (20% of federal) and child tax credit, and the 5% residential property tax credit (homeowners only). Check values: $40k: (40,000-2,850) x 4.95% = $1,838.93; $120k: $5,798.93. DISCREPANCIES WITH TAX FOUNDATION: none (4.95%, $2,850, $250k limit match).

phaseouts.applies_to: personal_exemption
phaseouts.formula: Exemption allowance = $2,850 if federal AGI <= $250,000 (single); $0 if federal AGI > $250,000 (cliff, not a phase-out). Irrelevant for $20k-$120k.

Illinois.changes_vs_2024: Personal exemption rose from $2,775 (2024, per IDOR Bulletin FY 2025-16) to $2,850 (2025): $3.71 less tax. Rate unchanged at 4.95%.

Indiana.notes: 2025 IT-40 line 8: 'multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)', where line 7 = federal AGI + Indiana add-backs - Indiana deductions - exemptions. Schedule 3 line 1: $1,000 personal exemption for a single filer (a deduction, even if claimed as a dependent elsewhere; additional exemptions for age 65+/blind/dependents not relevant). No standard deduction. No income phase-out of the $1,000 exemption. Starts from federal AGI (IT-40 line 1). Indiana conforms to the IRC as of 1/1/2023 and the 2025 booklet says it does not follow P.L. 119-21. That does not matter for wage earners: the federal tips/overtime deductions are below-AGI and never reach Indiana. Other items that matter at $20k-$120k: renter's deduction (Schedule 2 line 1) = lesser of rent paid or $3,000 for renters of a principal residence subject to Indiana property tax. It is widely available but renter-only, so it is excluded from the numbers; it is worth up to $90 state + $3,000 x county rate. Indiana EITC (10% of federal) excluded. Check values (wages = AGI, no renter's deduction): $40k: state tax $1,170.00; $120k: $3,570.00. LOCAL (county income tax, all 92 counties, Schedule CT-40): base is the same Indiana AGI after exemptions (IT-40 line 7). Rate is set by county of residence on Jan 1 (or county of principal work for out-of-state residents). Per the official 2025 Indiana County Income Tax Rates chart (back of 2025 Schedule CT-40), rates range from 0.50% (Porter) to 3.00% (Randolph), unweighted mean 1.914%, median 1.95% (my computation over all 92 counties). Marion (Indianapolis) is 2.02%, Allen 1.59%, Hamilton 1.10%, Lake 1.50%. typical_local_income_tax_rate is set to the Tax Foundation footnote (a) figure of 0.49% of AGI (2022 IRS/Census effective rate), as instructed. CAUTION: that figure is about 1/4 of the statutory county rates every resident pays (about 1.9% average; about 1.9% of AGI for a $40k single filer). I could not verify why TF's number is so low. My unverified guess is that the Census source classifies the state-administered county tax inconsistently. For a typical resident wage earner, 0.019 (unweighted county mean) or a population-weighted mean (not computed: no official population weights pulled) is far more defensible than 0.0049. DISCREPANCIES WITH TAX FOUNDATION: rate (3.0%) and exemption ($1,000) match. The local rate (0.49%) conflicts with the statutory county rates as explained above. COMPILER OVERRIDE OF THE LOCAL RATE: typical_local_income_tax_rate is set to 0.0174, the 2025 statutory county income tax rate averaged over all 92 counties weighted by Census Bureau Vintage 2024 county population estimates (POPESTIMATE2024; total 6,924,275), computed from the official 2025 Indiana County Income Tax Rates chart on Schedule CT-40 (forms.in.gov id=16902). Exact value 1.7440%; unweighted mean 1.914%, median 1.95%, range 0.50% (Porter) to 3.00% (Randolph). It is a statutory rate applied to the same base as the state tax (Indiana AGI after the $1,000 exemption), so for a $40k wage earner it equals about 1.70% of wages. It replaces the Tax Foundation footnote (a) figure of 0.49% of AGI, which is implausibly low given that every Indiana resident pays a county rate of at least 0.50%; the reason for the TF figure could not be determined. This is the only state where the field does not use the TF footnote (a) average.
Indiana.changes_vs_2024: State rate fell from 3.05% (2024; 2024 IT-40PNR line 8) to 3.0% (2025). Applied to Indiana AGI after the $1,000 exemption, that is $19.50 less at $40k wages. Personal exemption unchanged at $1,000. County rates changed for TY2025 in 10 counties (Decatur, Fayette, Floyd, Fulton, Gibson, Henry, Jay, Monroe, Rush, Switzerland; asterisked on the 2025 CT-40 chart). Statute sets 2.95% for 2026 (DN #1 effective 1/1/2026), not used here.

Iowa.notes: 2025 IA 1040: line 2 = federal taxable income (federal 1040 line 15); line 5 = 'Multiply line 4 by 3.8%'; Step 3 personal credit 1 x $40. 2025 Expanded Instructions: 'For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2023, the starting point for taxation is federal taxable income. Iowa has also adopted rolling conformity...' So Iowa's effective standard deduction = the federal standard deduction. For 2025 that is $15,750 single (IRS Form 1040 (2025), created 9/5/25, under P.L. 119-21), not $15,000. The 2025 IA 1040 (rev. 41-001b, 10/14/2025) has a new line 1f for the federal Schedule 1-A senior deduction, which confirms Iowa follows OBBBA. TIPS/OVERTIME: Iowa CONFORMS, with no decoupling. Federal 1040 line 15 already nets out Schedule 1-A deductions (line 13b: tips up to $25,000, overtime premium up to $12,500 single, car-loan interest, senior $6,000). IA 1040 Schedule 1 (2025) has no add-back for them, and the expanded instructions say Schedule 1-A deductions are already in federal taxable income. So Iowa taxable income = wages - 15,750 - any Schedule 1-A deductions. The $40 credit is nonrefundable. The low-income exemption ($9,000) and single-filer tax reduction worksheet are not binding at $20k+ (see phaseouts). Check values (no Schedule 1-A deductions): $20k: 3.8% x 4,250 - 40 = $121.50; $40k: $881.50; $80k: $2,401.50; $120k: $3,921.50. LOCAL: school district income surtax = a percentage of state tax after nonrefundable credits (IA 1040 line 18), by school district of residence on 12/31. 2025 rates run 0%-20% across 324 districts (37 at 0%), unweighted mean 5.4%, median 5%. Six counties (Appanoose, Cass, Pocahontas, Sac, Shelby, Winnebago) add a 1% EMS surtax included in the table. Weighting 2025 district rates by each district's 2024 surtax base (IDR 2024 School District Report) gives about 2.98% of state tax, or about 0.087% of total income (my computation). typical_local_income_tax_rate = Tax Foundation footnote (a) 0.09% of AGI (2022 data), which is consistent. At $40k wages a 5% surtax adds about $44 (0.11% of wages); the weighted average 3% adds about $26. Excluded: Iowa EITC (15% of federal). DISCREPANCIES WITH TAX FOUNDATION: TF lists the standard deduction as 'n.a.', but Iowa effectively uses the federal standard deduction via its federal-taxable-income starting point ($15,750 for 2025 after OBBBA; TF predates OBBBA). Rate 3.8% and $40 credit match.

phaseouts.applies_to: low_income_exemption_and_tax_reduction
phaseouts.formula: Single, not a dependent: no tax if income base <= $9,000 ($24,000 if 65+), where income base = Iowa taxable income + federal standard/itemized deduction (included in line 2) + federal Schedule 1-A senior deduction + QBI deduction + NOL carryover + lump-sum. Otherwise IA 1040 line 12 = min(tax after credits, income base - 9000) (2025 Income Tax Reduction Worksheet 41-146). Never binding at $20k+ wages.

Iowa.changes_vs_2024: Material. 2024 single schedule (2024 Tax Calculation Worksheet 41-026): 4.40% on $0-$6,210; 4.82% on $6,210-$31,050; 5.70% above. 2025 is a flat 3.8%. Because Iowa starts from federal taxable income, the embedded standard deduction rose from the 2024 federal $14,600 to the 2025 OBBBA federal $15,750. Under rolling conformity, the new federal Schedule 1-A deductions (qualified tips, qualified overtime, car-loan interest, senior deduction) also reduce Iowa taxable income in 2025. $40 personal exemption credit unchanged. At $40k wages: 2024 TI = 40,000 - 14,600 = 25,400, tax = 273.24 + 4.82% x 19,190 - 40 = $1,158.20; 2025 TI = 24,250, tax = 3.8% x 24,250 - 40 = $881.50.

Kansas.notes: 2025 Kansas Individual Income Tax booklet (ip25): K-40 line 1 federal AGI; line 4 standard deduction $3,605 single; line 5 exemption allowance $9,160 single (a deduction, not a credit); line 7 taxable income; 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet for single: $0-$23,000 x 5.2%; $23,001+ x 5.58% minus $87 (exact bracket arithmetic gives $87.40, so the worksheet differs from pure brackets by $0.40; tax table for TI < $100k). Standard deduction is NOT inflation-indexed: K.S.A. 79-32,119(c)(2) as amended by L. 2024 ch. 1 (Special Session) sets $3,605 single 'for tax year 2024, and all tax years thereafter' (the hint's assumption of indexing is incorrect). No income phase-out of SD or exemption. Value at $40k wages: TI = 40,000 - 3,605 - 9,160 = 27,235; tax = 1,196.00 + 5.58% x 4,235 = 1,432.31 (worksheet: 1,432.71). OBBBA tips/overtime are below federal AGI so do not affect Kansas; no Kansas subtraction for them in the 2025 booklet. No local income tax on wages (Tax Foundation footnote (a) notes some KS jurisdictions tax interest/dividend income only). Credits not included: KS EITC = 17% of federal EITC (refundable per worksheet); child/dependent care credit. Matches Tax Foundation exactly.
Kansas.changes_vs_2024: None material. 2024 (SB 1, 2024 special session, retroactive to 1/1/2024) and 2025 are identical: 5.2% on taxable income to $23,000 and 5.58% above (single), standard deduction $3,605, exemption allowance $9,160. Only change: the food sales tax credit (nonrefundable $125/exemption, FAGI <= $30,615) appears in the 2024 booklet but not the 2025 booklet; it never applied to a single filer under 55, not blind/disabled, with no dependent child.

Kentucky.notes: The 2025 Form 740 packet (42A740(PKT) (10-25)), 'What's New', says: for 2025 the standard deduction is $3,270 and the individual income tax rate is 4%. Computation: federal AGI (Form 740 line 5) plus Schedule M additions, minus subtractions, gives KY AGI. Subtract the $3,270 standard deduction and multiply by 4%. Kentucky has no personal exemption. Personal tax credits exist only for 65+, blind, or Kentucky National Guard, so they are 0 for this profile. Federal income tax is not deductible. Conformity: HB 775 (2025) set the IRC reference date to 12/31/2024. The 2025 instructions say explicitly that qualified tips, overtime income, and car loan interest are not deductible on the Kentucky return. The Family Size Tax Credit (see phaseouts) matters only at the bottom of the range. At $20k wages, tax is $669.20, the credit is 20% ($133.84), and net is about $535. From about $20,815 of MGI up there is no credit. Illustrative 2025 state tax: $40k = $1,469.20; $80k = $3,069.20; $120k = $4,669.20. Local occupational license taxes, which are levied on gross wages, generally by place of work, are widespread and are not in the state numbers. typical_local_income_tax_rate uses the Tax Foundation footnote (a) statewide average effective local rate of 1.31% of AGI (2022 IRS/Census data). Statutory examples: Louisville Metro (Jefferson Co.) is 2.2% for residents (of which 0.75% goes to the Louisville and Anchorage public school boards) and 1.45% for nonresidents, who do not pay the school board portion (LMRC 2025 OL-3D instructions, verified from the PDF). Lexington-Fayette is 2.25% of gross wages earned in Fayette County, withheld by employers. That rate comes from the LFUCG occupational license page as indexed by search; a direct fetch of lexingtonky.gov/node/659 returned 404 on 2026-10-17. Other city, county and school-district rates vary and were not compiled. Credits not included: the child and dependent care credit (20% of federal) needs a dependent. No discrepancies with Tax Foundation (TF: 4.0%, $3,270).

phaseouts.applies_to: Family Size Tax Credit (nonrefundable, a percentage of Form 740 line 19 tax). Family size 1 means a single filer with no qualifying children.

params.bands_note: each pair is [not-over upper bound, credit pct]; above 20,815 the credit is 0

Kentucky.changes_vs_2024: Rate is 4% in both years. Standard deduction rose from $3,160 (2024, per the 2024 740-NP packet) to $3,270. The Family Size Tax Credit threshold for family size 1 rose from $15,060 to $15,650, and the zero-credit point moved from MGI $20,030 to $20,815. At $20,000 wages the credit is 10% in 2024 vs 20% in 2025. Net effect at $40k wages: -$4.40 (the standard deduction change times 4%).

Louisiana.notes: 2025 IT-540: Line 7 is federal AGI (1040 line 11b), adjusted on Schedule E for Louisiana exclusions. Line 8 is the standard deduction: $12,500 for single/MFS, $25,000 for MFJ/QSS/HoH. Line 9D adds excess federal itemized deductions for itemizers only: the federal medical and dental deduction above $15,750 for single filers. Line 10 is Louisiana taxable income. Line 11 is Line 10 x .03, rounded to the nearest dollar. No personal exemption remains for a single filer with no dependents (Act 11 replaced the combined exemption and deduction with the standard deduction and repealed the additional exemptions). No line deducts federal income tax; Line 10 is FAGI minus the standard deduction minus excess itemized deductions only. Background, not re-verified in this pass: the federal income tax deduction was eliminated starting tax year 2022. RIB 25-012 says the standard deduction is CPI-U indexed starting 1/1/2026, so it is the flat $12,500 for 2025. Tips and overtime: the 2025 instructions have no Louisiana subtraction for the federal no-tax-on-tips or overtime deductions. Those federal deductions sit below AGI, so they do not reach Louisiana's federal-AGI starting point. Credits not included in the numbers: the Louisiana EIC (refundable, 5% of federal EIC) and the refundable child care credit (FAGI <= $25,000, needs a dependent). Louisiana has no local income taxes. Illustrative 2025 tax: $20k = $225; $40k = $825; $80k = $2,025; $120k = $3,225. The instructions PDF used is LDR's 'IT540i-WEB-2025-Revised-7-26' file (revised 2026). Its rate and deduction instructions match the 2025 IT-540 form face (IT540WEB-BC(2025) F). No discrepancies with Tax Foundation (TF: 3%, $12,500).
Louisiana.changes_vs_2024: Major change (Act 11 of the 2024 3rd Ext. Sess., effective for tax periods beginning on or after 1/1/2025). 2024 single rates were 1.85% on $0-$12,500, 3.5% on $12,501-$50,000 and 4.25% over $50,000, with a combined personal exemption-standard deduction of $4,500 (single) taken out of the lowest bracket first. The additional $1,000 exemptions for 65+, blind, and dependents also applied. 2025 is a flat 3% after a $12,500 standard deduction, with the additional exemptions repealed. Illustrative at $40k federal AGI, computed from RIB 25-012 parameters: 2024 about $1,111 (1.85% x $8,000 + 3.5% x $27,500) vs 2025 $825. The tax falls at every point in the $20k-$120k range.

Maine.notes: Rates/brackets: MRS '2025 Rates' schedule (prepared Feb 3, 2026), Schedule #1 single: < $26,800 at 5.8%; $26,800 to < $63,450 is $1,554 + 6.75% of excess; >= $63,450 is $4,028 + 7.15% of excess. This matches TF. Standard deduction: $15,000 single, NOT the OBBBA $15,750. Maine conforms to the IRC as of Dec 31, 2024, and the Governor's directive decoupled from the OBBBA standard-deduction increase. This was later codified: 36 M.R.S. § 5124-C(1-B) sets the TY2025 basic standard deduction at $15,000 single (P.L. 2025, c. 650, Pt. K, § 13 [L.D. 2212] and P.L. 2025, c. 752, § 1 [L.D. 705], effective July 29, 2026, per MRS '2026 Tax Law Changes'). TY2026 is $15,700. From 2027 it equals the federal amount. Standard deduction phase-out (1040ME line 17 worksheet; Maine AGI = 1040ME line 16): if MAGI > $100,000 single, fraction = min(1, (MAGI - 100,000)/75,000), rounded to 4 decimals, and deduction = 15,000 x (1 - fraction). Fully phased out at $175,000. Value at $40k: $15,000. At $120k: fraction 0.2667, deduction = 15,000 - 4,000.50 = $10,999.50 (about $11,000). Personal exemption: $5,150 deduction (line 18). It phases out above Maine AGI $333,450 single over a $125,000 range, which does not bind in range. TF footnote (y) shows $323,900, the 2024 figure. Starting point: federal AGI (1040ME line 14) +/- Maine modifications. OBBBA tip/overtime deductions are below the federal AGI line, so they never enter Maine income. Examples: at $40k wages, taxable = 40,000 - 15,000 - 5,150 = 19,850 and tax = $1,151. At $120k, taxable = 120,000 - 10,999.50 - 5,150 = 103,850.50 and tax = $4,028 + 7.15% x 40,400.50 = $6,917. MRS also publishes 2025 tax tables; tax from the table differs from the schedule only by rounding. Not included, but relevant at the low end: refundable Sales Tax Fairness Credit (single total income <= $32,950; maximum $280 depending on dependents), refundable Property Tax Fairness Credit (depends on rent/property tax), and Maine EITC. The Maine Affordability Payment ($300 one-time, single FAGI < $50,000, filing a 2025 return) is a payment program, not an income-tax parameter. The 2% surcharge on income over $1M starts TY2026 and is irrelevant here. No local income tax. Discrepancies with TF: the TF values for brackets, $15,000 standard deduction, $5,150 exemption and the $100,000 phase-out start all match 2025. Only the personal-exemption phase-out threshold in TF footnote (y) is stale ($323,900 vs $333,450).
Maine.changes_vs_2024: Inflation indexing. 2024 single schedule: 5.8% < $26,050; 6.75% $26,050-$61,600; 7.15% >= $61,600. 2025: $26,800 and $63,450. Standard deduction $14,600 (2024, equal to federal) to $15,000 (2025, fixed in statute at the pre-OBBBA federal amount). Personal exemption $5,000 to $5,150. All three changes slightly lower tax across $20k-$120k. The 2024 standard-deduction phase-out threshold was not re-verified.

Maryland.notes: Source: Maryland 2025 Resident Tax Booklet (Comptroller), Instruction 17, Tax Rate Schedule I (Single/MFS/Dependent): $1-1,000 2%; $1,001-2,000 $20 + 3%; $2,001-3,000 $50 + 4%; $3,001-100,000 $90 + 4.75%; $100,001-125,000 $4,697.50 + 5%; $125,001-150,000 $5,947.50 + 5.25%; $150,001-250,000 $7,260 + 5.5%; $250,001-500,000 $12,760 + 5.75%; $500,001-1,000,000 $27,135 + 6.25%; > $1,000,000 $58,385 + 6.5%. The base amounts equal the cumulative marginal tax. The tax table is required if TI < $100,000 (midpoint; small differences). This schedule is confirmed by the Comptroller Tax Alert (rev. Dec 22, 2025). Standard deduction (Instruction 16): flat $3,350 for single/MFS/dependent ($6,700 MFJ/HOH/QSS), with no income-based phase-in. Personal exemption: a $3,200 deduction, reduced by FEDERAL AGI (see phaseouts; $3,200 at $20k-$100k and $1,600 at $120k). Income starts from federal AGI, plus MD additions and minus subtractions, to give MD AGI. Federal tax is not deductible. Minimum filing level (single, under 65): $15,750 gross income. Examples (wages only, state tax): $20k: TI 13,450, $586.38. $40k: TI 33,450, $1,536.38. $80k: TI 73,450, $3,436.38. $120k: exemption 1,600, TI 115,050, $5,450. State EITC and poverty level credits are not included. LOCAL (applies to essentially all residents; base = Maryland taxable net income, the same base as the state tax). 2025 Local Tax Rate Chart: 3.20% in Baltimore City, Baltimore Co., Calvert, Caroline, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset and Wicomico; 3.30% Dorchester; 3.06% Harford; 3.03% Allegany, Carroll and Charles; 2.95% Washington; 2.74% Cecil; 2.65% Garrett; 2.40% Talbot; 2.25% Worcester (and nonresidents). Graduated, single: Anne Arundel 2.70% of TNI <= $50,000, $1,350 + 2.94% to $400,000, then 3.20%; Frederick 2.25% to $25,000, 2.75% to $50,000, 2.96% to $150,000, 3.20% above. The most common statutory rate is 3.20% (12 of 24 jurisdictions, including Montgomery, Prince George's, Baltimore County, Baltimore City and Howard). No population-weighted average was found in the Comptroller/DLS sources reviewed. typical_local_income_tax_rate = 0.0251 per the Tax Foundation footnote (a) statewide average effective rate as a percentage of AGI (2022 data). For comparison, 3.20% x TNI at $40k wages = $1,070, which is 2.68% of AGI. 2025 law raised the local cap to 3.30% (Dorchester for 2025; Kent 3.30% and Allegany 3.20% for 2026 per the Comptroller alert). Differences from Tax Foundation: TF shows a $2,700 standard deduction (2024 15%-of-AGI formula) instead of $3,350, and omits the 6.25%/6.5% brackets. The TF exemption ($3,200) and footnote (aa) phase-out range match.
Maryland.changes_vs_2024: Material. (1) The standard deduction changed from 15% of MD AGI (min $1,800, max $2,700 single; 2024 amounts per the Tax Foundation table, footnote z) to a flat $3,350, under the BRFA of 2025 (HB 352, Ch. 604). The income-based phase-in was eliminated and future amounts are COLA-indexed. At $40k+ wages that is +$650 of deduction, about -$31 state and -$21 local tax at 3.2%. At $20k the 2024 deduction was also capped at $2,700 (15% x 20,000 = 3,000). (2) New 6.25% bracket above $500,000 and 6.5% above $1,000,000; the 2024 top rate was 5.75% above $250,000. Irrelevant at <= $120k. (3) New 2% tax on net capital gain for FAGI > $350,000; itemized deductions reduced by 7.5% of FAGI above $200,000. (4) Local rates: Calvert 3.00% to 3.20%, St. Mary's 3.00% to 3.20%, Dorchester 3.20% to 3.30% (retroactive), Cecil 2.75% to 2.74%, and the Anne Arundel middle bracket rose to 2.94% (prior-year value not verified from an official document here). The personal exemption ($3,200) and the $100k phase-out start are unchanged.

phaseouts.applies_to: Personal exemption (Exemption Amount Chart 10A), by FEDERAL AGI, single or married filing separately
phaseouts.formula: exemption per exemption = 3200 if FAGI <= 100000; 1600 if 100000 < FAGI <= 125000; 800 if 125000 < FAGI <= 150000; 0 if FAGI > 150000. The $1,000 age-65/blind exemptions are not reduced.

Massachusetts.notes: Rates: DOR 'Tax Rates' page (mass.gov, updated Dec 30, 2025) lists 5.00% on wages and other Part B income, plus an extra 4% surtax on income over $1,083,150 for TY2025, so 9% combined above that (TF shows the same). Personal exemption: $4,400 single (Form 1 line 2a; mass.gov exemptions page). It is subtracted from income, so it works like a deduction. No standard deduction. Starting point is Massachusetts gross income under MA law (wages from W-2 box 16 on Form 1 line 3), not federal AGI. MA generally conforms to the IRC as of Jan 1, 2024, with specific auto-conforming provisions, and does not adopt OBBBA (P.L. 119-21) changes generally. The new federal tips/overtime deductions are irrelevant because MA does not start from federal figures. Every wage earner gets a deduction for amounts paid to Social Security, Medicare, Railroad, U.S. or Massachusetts retirement systems (Form 1 line 11): employee FICA withheld per W-2, capped at $2,000 per person. For a private-sector wage earner this is min(0.0765 x wages, 2000), which hits the cap at wages >= $26,144. Example: $1,530 at $20k wages, $2,000 at $40k and $120k. IRA/SEP/SIMPLE contributions are not deductible. Optional renter deduction (line 14): 50% of rent on an MA principal residence, max $4,000 per return. Not applied by default; see other_deductions. Low-income rules, irrelevant at >= $20k wages: No Tax Status if MA AGI (Line 27 worksheet) <= $8,000 single. Limited Income Credit if single MA AGI is between $8,000 and $14,000: tax is capped at 10% x (MA AGI - $8,000). Tax tables apply when line 21 < $24,000 (5% at table midpoints); otherwise 5% x line 21. Example at $40k wages: taxable = 40,000 - 2,000 - 4,400 = 33,600; tax = $1,680. PFML is a payroll contribution, not income tax, and is not deductible. Per the 2025 Form 1 instructions (line 49), the 2025 wage cap is $176,100 and the maximum employee contribution is $810.06, which implies an employee rate of 0.46% of eligible wages. The self-employed opt-in maximum of $1,549.68 implies a total rate of 0.88%. MA EITC (a percentage of the federal EITC) is not included. No local income taxes. Source caveat: mass.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated PDF downloads. The 2025 Form 1 instructions were read from an NBER mirror of the DOR file (PDF metadata: Author 'Massachusetts Department of Revenue', Title '2025 Massachusetts Form 1 instruction booklet', modified Jan 30, 2026). Rate, surtax threshold and $4,400 exemption were confirmed directly on official mass.gov HTML pages. No discrepancies with Tax Foundation. Structure label: coded 'graduated' (as Tax Foundation classifies it) because of the 4% surtax bracket above $1,083,150; for wages of $20k-$120k the tax is a flat 5% of Part B taxable income.
Massachusetts.changes_vs_2024: None material at $20k-$120k. Rate 5.0%, single personal exemption $4,400, $2,000 FICA/retirement deduction cap and No Tax Status/Limited Income Credit thresholds are the same as 2024. Only change: the 4% surtax threshold rose from $1,053,750 (2024) to $1,083,150 (2025).

other_deductions.name: FICA / public retirement contributions deduction (Form 1 line 11)
other_deductions.formula: min(employee_social_security_tax + employee_medicare_tax (or MA/US public retirement contributions), 2000)

other_deductions.name: Rental deduction (Form 1 line 14), optional; renters only

phaseouts.applies_to: tax_liability (No Tax Status / Limited Income Credit; single)
phaseouts.formula: if MA_AGI <= 8000: tax = 0; elif MA_AGI <= 14000: tax = min(regular_tax, 0.10 * (MA_AGI - 8000)); else regular_tax

Michigan.notes: 2025 MI-1040 book p.2: 'The income tax rate for 2025 is 4.25 percent'; 'personal and stillbirth exemption allowances are $5,800'. The 2025 Taxpayer Assistance Manual has the same figures plus a prior-year table (2021-2024 rate 4.25/4.25/4.05/4.25%, exemption $4,900/$5,000/$5,400/$5,600). The exemption is a deduction from taxable income, with no income phase-out. No standard deduction for non-seniors (the Michigan standard deduction applies only to certain retirees by birth year). Starts from federal AGI. Tips/overtime: 2025 PA 24 (signed 10/7/2025) adds MCL 206.30 deductions mirroring federal IRC 224/225 only 'for tax years beginning after December 31, 2025 and before January 1, 2029' (Treasury notice 1/6/2026). There is no Michigan tips/overtime deduction for 2025, and since they are below-AGI federally they do not reduce Michigan AGI either. Excluded credits: Michigan EITC (30% of federal) and the Homestead Property Tax Credit (income-tested, open to renters and owners, total household resources limit). Check values (wages = AGI): $40k: (40,000-5,800) x 4.25% = $1,453.50; $120k: $4,853.50. LOCAL: 24 cities levy a city income tax under the Uniform City Income Tax Ordinance. Per the 2025 TAM p.99, 20 cities use 1% resident / 0.5% nonresident (Albion, Battle Creek, Benton Harbor, Big Rapids, East Lansing, Flint, Grayling, Hamtramck, Hudson, Ionia, Jackson, Lansing, Lapeer, Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Pontiac, Port Huron, Portland, Springfield, Walker). Alternate rates: Detroit 2.4% resident / 1.2% nonresident; Grand Rapids 1.5% / 0.75%; Highland Park 2% / 1%; Saginaw 1.5% / 0.75%. City taxes have their own exemptions and bases (not verified here). typical_local_income_tax_rate = Tax Foundation footnote (a) statewide average 0.18% of AGI (2022 data). DISCREPANCIES WITH TAX FOUNDATION: none (4.25%, $5,800 match).
Michigan.changes_vs_2024: Personal exemption rose from $5,600 (2024) to $5,800 (2025): $8.50 less tax. Rate unchanged at 4.25% (2024 also 4.25%; only 2023 used the temporary 4.05%). No other change that matters at $20k-$120k for a non-senior single wage earner. The new state tips/overtime deductions (2025 PA 24) start in TY2026, not 2025.

Minnesota.notes: 2025 Form M1 instructions (last updated 12/5/2025): line 1 = federal AGI (Form 1040 line 11a); SD $14,950 single; Tax Rate Schedule (single): 0-32,570 at 5.35%; 32,570-106,990: $1,742.50 + 6.80%; 106,990-198,630: $6,803.06 + 7.85%; over 198,630: $13,996.80 + 9.85% (tax table required below $86,800). No personal exemption for the filer (only a $5,200 dependent exemption). SD phase-out (irrelevant at $20k-$120k): if AGI > $238,950, reduce SD by the lesser of [3% x (min(AGI,330,300) - 238,950) + 10% x max(0, AGI - 330,300)] or 80% of SD. Value at $40k wages: TI 25,050 x 5.35% = $1,340.18. Minnesota conforms to the IRC as amended through May 1, 2023; H.R. 1 (OBBBA) adjustments are made on Schedule M1NC, but because MN starts from federal AGI the OBBBA below-the-line tips/overtime/senior/car-loan deductions do not reduce MN income. No local income tax. Credits not included: Working Family Credit (EITC-type), Child Tax Credit, Renter's Credit (Schedule M1RENT; refundable, based on rent paid and household income - can be material for low-income renters). 1% NIIT-style surtax on investment income > $1M irrelevant. Matches Tax Foundation exactly.
